summary: Session 4 shipped the close-out obligations as a serialized projection and finished the `<- here` removal in TypeScript. `close_preflight --write` runs the report exactly as before (same stdout, same exit code) and additionally serializes `PreflightReport.to_dict()` VERBATIM to `<set>/.dabbler/close-obligations.json`, with a SHA-256 per top-level file of the session-set directory and a git fingerprint beside it; `--check` compares without evaluating (exit 0 fresh, 3 otherwise). The Work Explorer reads that file and renders a Close-out row under the in-flight session, expanding to one row per obligation. The preflight costs 2-7 seconds, so the renderer never calls it -- the file is the whole interface, which is the pattern Set 120 S3 established. Four decisions were journaled before any code: the projection is an ignored per-machine cache under the already-ignored `.dabbler/` (a tracked file written mid-session would stale its own verification round and buy a metered backstop round at close -- the failure Sets 111 S2, 112 S3 and 114 S1 each paid for); freshness is TWO questions, because no content digest can speak for a predicate that reads git; the obligations are one grouped row rather than fourteen flat ones; and the marker removal is the whole derivation rather than the two sites the spec names. The marker half deleted `HERE_MARKER` and its render site, `markHere`, `TERMINAL_STATUSES` and `StepRow.isHere`, stripped `isHere` from the shared parity corpus, and replaced the two Python guards Set 120 S3 left behind to hold that field alive -- so both halves compare the same whole row again and the corpus's declared divergence is over. What an operator reads instead is the in-progress glyph on the step whose RECORDED status is in-progress. The end-of-set multi-provider path-aware critique (gpt-5.6-sol + gemini-3.1-pro, each reading the repo) returned five Major findings and every one was real: the volatility rule was derived from a source-text scan for a direct `_run_git` call and so missed `verification_integrity` (an evidence stamp binding the repo-wide work diff) and `test_run_fresh` (a run-of-record digest over covered source) -- fixed by INVERTING the default so `SET_LOCAL_CHECKS` names the set-local checks and everything else is volatile, guarded by an AST walk that follows function-local imports; a damaged payload degraded into a short confident list -- now any structural damage reads `unreadable` and only ENOENT reads `absent`; the group row could paint the done glyph on an `undecided-backstop-would-route` verdict -- now done requires fresh AND nothing outstanding AND a settled verdict; the file watcher did not cover the projection, so the row would not move after the very command the UAT walk prescribes; and the reader's dirent check diverged from the writer's `os.path.isfile` on symlinks, which would have pinned the panel at stale forever. At the UAT walk the operator ruled `Open Session Artifacts` out of the session menu; it was removed WHOLESALE (command, manifest entries, registry entry, discovery helpers, its Layer 2 suite and its two Layer 3 scenarios) because the command was palette-hidden by design and the menu was its only door -- replaced by absence assertions at both layers. That removal made an empty context menu reachable for the first time, which the full Layer 3 run caught as a real defect in `rowContextMenuText`; the helper now treats 'no menu' as an answer and the spec asserts the menu is empty rather than merely lacking two labels. Verification: discovery ISSUES_FOUND (1 Major -- Playwright-scoped changes after the last recorded full run), supplementary clean, remediation-review round 3 ISSUES_FOUND (1 Major -- the same class one suite over: mocha run but not recorded), remediation-review round 4 VERIFIED with both fixes accepted and zero findings. Both blocking findings were the gap between running a suite and recording it, and neither was a defect in shipped code.

uat.attestation: Operator walked the whole set on 2026-08-11 and answered every item in s4-uat-walk.md in place. All five looks passed: session rows read as 'titles someone wrote'; left-click lands on the right session's block without scrolling; the run prompt is offered on the row they would have picked; the step in flight is identifiable by icon alone; the close-out row and its regeneration are 'fine'. Three decisions ratified: keep the obligations grouped, keep the projection git-ignored, and agreed that the in-progress icon is enough now that the marker is gone. One change ruled at the walk -- 'we no longer need Open Session Artifacts' -- and it was removed from the session menu in this session, wholesale.
